oxide-capabilities-security:3.limits: 100 native field records; native enumeration only visits AcroForm-linked fields. Independent inventory reconciles PDF object identities against AcroForm /V references. Unlinked objects, duplicate references, direct dictionaries, malformed or repeated field links and native/reference-count mismatch produce partial status. oxide-capabilities-security:3.known_failure: Ordinary zero-padded /Contents is rejected as trailing DER data; this cryptographically valid fixture remains an explicit partial/unverifiable result. oxide-capabilities-security:4.limits: 100 blobs/category and 1 MiB total; report hashes/sizes only, no certificate or revocation blobs exported. Presence and PAdES classification are not cryptographic trust validation. has_document_timestamp is a presence signal.

oxide-capabilities-security:5.limits: Only public DER certificates already embedded in the input PDF DSS are parsed. No arbitrary certificate-file or credential-store access. is_valid checks the time window only; trust chains and revocation remain not checked. Certificate has no public direct constructor in the binding; loading occurs through the static loader.

oxide-capabilities-security:6.limits: At most 100 existing PDF DocTimeStamp dictionaries and 1 MiB token bytes. Read-only parse and token selfcheck, without TSA/network access. Bare TSTInfo metadata parsing is tested; its signature verification remains unsupported without a CMS wrapper. Even a valid token signature does not verify the PDF byte-range imprint, certificate trust or revocation. Positive CMS timestamp-token selfcheck remains unqualified.
